taxonomic_note: Strict Opuntia phaeacantha is accepted, but older broad phaeacantha treatments included material now separated as O. gilvescens, O. camanchica, O. spinosibacca, and related concepts.
look_here_first: Use the brown-spine/desert pricklypear concept cautiously: low to spreading pads, usually conspicuous brown-gray spines, yellow flowers often with reddish bases, and fleshy reddish-purple fruit. Confirm the modern taxon concept before trusting old Central Texas labels.

project_inclusion.target_zone_status: UNRESOLVED TAXON CONCEPT — USER APPROVED LEARNER INCLUSION
project_inclusion.range_basis: Historical Hays/Travis labels are retained as concept evidence only because the modern split may reassign old broad-name material. Williamson is outside the target zone.

approval_exception.reason: Private learner inclusion is allowed while the taxon/range HOLD remains explicit.

best_field_traits: pads used together with spine pattern
usually conspicuous brown to gray spines
yellow flowers often with reddish bases
morphology_keys.comparison_training: These are field-concept cues, not permission to transfer historical broad-name records. Modern taxon identity must still be checked against O. gilvescens, O. camanchica, and related split taxa.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use a complete pad/spine/flower/fruit suite and modern expert-identified references. Old 'phaeacantha' labels are not sufficient.

diagnostic_image_needs: flower showing reddish base if present
